horizon_risk.caveat: Block-bootstrap simulation of the real P2-governed 6-leg ladder (same compute_sizing() the live watchdogs call), NOT a live-account realized track record. mdd_*_pct_of_equity is the key read: the dollar MDD generally grows as the ladder scales up, but it shrinks as a SHARE of the (also-growing) account -- that's the 'getting safer as we scale' effect, and where it stops improving is worth watching, not assuming. The _k05 columns are the frozen surplus-aggression overlay candidate (P0=$50k, B=$20k, k=0.5 -- same policy scripts/compute_p2_sizing.py actually deploys live), run on the SAME sampled paths as the plain-P2 columns so they're directly comparable. The real underlying data pool is ~3.25 years (818 trading days); horizons beyond that (48/60 months) are block-bootstrap resampling of that same pool, not additional real history -- treat them as a longer extrapolation under the same statistical assumptions, with correspondingly less confidence than the shorter horizons. Where level_capped is true, the median path's ladder qty has hit MAX_LEVEL (a sanity ceiling against a misparsed equity read, not a real policy cap) -- that row understates the formula's own growth AND implies a contract count far past any real broker/market capacity question, so treat it as 'the model ran out of room,' not a real projection.
